name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
founded_year_range: 1992-2002 (developed 1992-99; first RCT 2000; Guilford manual 2002; 2nd ed. Oct 2012, ©2013)
cost_summary: mbct.com and mindfulmood.org post no prices. Posted 2026 fees for 8-week online courses: UC San Diego MBCT USD 595 (USD 545 if paid early); UMass Memorial MBSR or MBCT USD 650; Oxford Mindfulness Foundation MBCT-L GBP 300. Free on the UK NHS. Self-help book (The Mindful Way Through Depression, 2nd ed.) USD 23.95. The protocol is not proprietary.
mechanism_summary: After recovery from depression, mild dysphoria can reactivate depressogenic thinking (cognitive reactivity). Rumination and experiential avoidance ("doing mode") then drive relapse. MBCT trains decentering and metacognitive awareness ("thoughts are not facts") and a "being mode", so people notice early warning signs and disengage. The theoretical basis is Teasdale's ICS model. MBCT claims no central neurological or autonomic cause of somatic illness. Adaptations for pain and health anxiety apply the same reactivity model to aversive sensations.
techniques: 8 weekly 2-2.25 h group sessions plus a practice day
about 45 min a day of home practice with audio
digital Mindful Mood Balance (8 online sessions over 3 months with minimal coaching)
mainstream_notes: NICE recommended MBCT for recurrent depression (3+ episodes) in CG23 (2004) and CG90 (2009). NG222 (2022), recs 1.8.5-1.8.6: for remitted people at higher risk of relapse, consider group CBT or MBCT (usually 8 sessions over 2-3 months) instead of or alongside continued antidepressants. NG222 Table 1 lists group mindfulness and meditation (e.g., MBCT) as an option for less severe depression, 7th of 11 options (verified 2026-10-13). MBCT is delivered in NHS Talking Therapies and secondary care, and the Oxford 'MBCT for Depression' course is for UK residents with a GP. Mindful Nation UK (APPG, 2015) recommended commissioning MBCT for 15% of the 580,000 adults a year at risk of recurrence (87,000 a year, about GBP 10M a year) and training 100 NHS MBCT teachers a year, noting that access was 'still extremely limited'. Kaiser Permanente Colorado hosted the 460-person digital trial. Teacher training runs at Oxford, Bangor, UCSD and Toronto.
insurance_notes: Free through the UK NHS. In the US it can be billed as group psychotherapy (e.g., CPT 90853) when a licensed clinician delivers it; there is no MBCT-specific code. Community or lay-teacher courses are self-pay.

key_trials.citation: Teasdale JD, Segal ZV, Williams JM et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2000;68:615-23 (PMID 10965637)
key_trials.design: RCT, MBCT+TAU vs TAU, recovered recurrent depression
key_trials.finding: Over 60 weeks, relapse fell for patients with 3+ prior episodes (77% of the sample) but not for those with 2

key_trials.citation: Ma SH, Teasdale JD. J Consult Clin Psychol 2004;72:31-40 (PMID 14756612)
key_trials.finding: Replicated the relapse reduction for 3+ episodes

key_trials.citation: Kuyken W et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2008;76:966-78 (PMID 19045965)
key_trials.design: RCT, MBCT with support to taper antidepressants vs maintenance antidepressants
key_trials.finding: Relapse over 15 months 47% vs 60% (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.39-1.04, ns); MBCT better on residual symptoms, comorbidity and quality of life; 75% fully discontinued antidepressants

key_trials.citation: Segal ZV et al. Arch Gen Psychiatry 2010;67:1256-64 (PMID 21135325)
key_trials.design: 3-arm RCT, MBCT vs maintenance antidepressants vs placebo, in remitters (160 treated acutely, 84 remitted and randomized)
key_trials.finding: In unstable remitters, MBCT and antidepressants both cut relapse hazard by 73% vs placebo; no difference in stable remitters

key_trials.citation: Williams JM et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2014;82:275-86 (PMID 24294837)
key_trials.design: Dismantling RCT, MBCT vs cognitive psychoeducation vs TAU
key_trials.finding: No significant overall effect on relapse over 12 months (HR 0.88 [0.58-1.35] vs CPE, 0.69 [0.42-1.12] vs TAU); benefit only with above-median childhood trauma

key_trials.design: Single-blind RCT, MBCT with antidepressant taper vs maintenance antidepressants, 95 UK general practices
key_trials.finding: MBCT not superior: HR 0.89 (0.67-1.18) over 24 months; outcomes similar in both arms

key_trials.citation: Huijbers MJ et al. (MOMENT) Br J Psychiatry 2016;208:366-73 (PMID 26892847)
key_trials.design: Non-inferiority RCT, MBCT then antidepressant discontinuation vs MBCT + continued antidepressants
key_trials.finding: Non-inferiority not shown; relapse was higher and came sooner after discontinuation

key_trials.citation: Kuyken W et al. JAMA Psychiatry 2016;73:565-74 (PMID 27119968)
key_trials.design: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 9 RCTs
key_trials.finding: Relapse HR 0.69 (0.58-0.82) vs no MBCT and 0.79 (0.64-0.97) vs active treatments over 60 weeks; some evidence (no significant formal interaction) of a larger effect with higher baseline severity

key_trials.citation: McManus F et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2012;80:817-28 (PMID 22708977)
key_trials.design: RCT, MBCT + usual services vs usual services, health anxiety
key_trials.finding: ITT d=0.48 on health anxiety at post and 1 year; diagnosis retained by 36% vs 76% at 1 year

key_trials.citation: Farb N et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2018;86:200-4 (PMID 29265831)
key_trials.design: RCT, MBCT (n=82) vs cognitive therapy (n=84) for relapse prevention in remitted MDD
key_trials.finding: No difference in relapse rate or time to relapse over 24 months

key_trials.citation: Segal ZV, Dimidjian S et al. JAMA Psychiatry 2020;77:563-73 (PMID 31995132)
key_trials.design: RCT, online Mindful Mood Balance + usual care vs usual care, Kaiser Colorado, residual depressive symptoms
key_trials.finding: Small PHQ-9 advantage (~1 point), more remission, relapse HR 0.61 (0.39-0.95); no difference in physical functioning

key_trials.citation: Dimidjian S et al. J Consult Clin Psychol 2016;84:134-45 (PMID 26654212)
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, perinatal MBCT (MBCT-PD, n=43) vs TAU (n=43), pregnant women with depression history

key_trials.citation: Day MA et al. Clin J Pain 2014;30:152-61 (PMID 23446085)
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, MBCT for headache vs delayed treatment
key_trials.finding: Feasible; ITT gains in pain self-efficacy and acceptance (d=0.82); pain interference improved only in completers

key_trials.citation: Day MA et al. Pain Med 2019;20:2134-48 (PMID 30605517)
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, MBCT vs mindfulness meditation vs cognitive therapy, chronic low back pain
key_trials.finding: All arms improved with no between-group differences post-treatment; at follow-up MBCT beat meditation on some outcomes

key_trials.citation: Bindicsova I et al. J Pain 2025;32:105429 (PMID 40379069)
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, 4-week self-directed internet MBCT vs delayed treatment, chronic pain
key_trials.finding: Feasible (88% retention); within-group pain interference improved (d=0.48), pain intensity changed little (d=0.20); no between-group efficacy test reported

controversy: Most pivotal trials were run by the developers. They earn Guilford royalties and training income, and Segal and Dimidjian disclose cofounding Mindful Noggin, Inc. The dismantling trial (Williams 2014) found no overall benefit over an active control. Farb 2018 found no difference from cognitive therapy. PREVENT was a non-superiority result that the media spun as "as good as pills". MOMENT found that stopping antidepressants after MBCT raised relapse. Benefit is concentrated in people with 3+ episodes. Meditation can have adverse effects: Britton et al. 2021 (PMID 35174010) found negative impacts on functioning in 37% of 96 MBCT participants and lasting bad effects in 6-14%. Evidence for pain is limited to small MBCT pilots (Day et al.; Bindicsova 2025, an internet MBCT pilot with N=48), and there are no trials of MBCT in ME/CFS, POTS, MCS, long COVID or FND.

indicators.value: Guilford manual (1st ed. 2002; 2nd ed. 2012/13); more than 70,000 in print
The Mindful Way Through Depression: more than 475,000 in print (2nd ed. 2024)
Recommended for recurrent depression (CG23), retained in CG90; NG222 2022 recs 1.8.5-1.8.6 (relapse prevention)
Mindfulness: Finding Peace in a Frantic World (Williams & Penman), more than 2 million copies sold (publisher claim)

indicators.metric: Lancet PREVENT trial plus Mindful Nation UK parliamentary report

indicators.value: Mindful Mood Balance, N=460 at Kaiser

popularity.reach_estimate: Publisher figures give more than 2.5 million book copies (Finding Peace over 2M, Mindful Way over 475k, manual over 70k). Course completers are probably in the hundreds of thousands worldwide, but no enrolment totals are published. Cumulative exposure is roughly 10^6-10^7.
popularity.method_notes: Trajectory is anchored on documented milestones: first RCT 2000, manual 2002, NICE 2004, self-help books 2007/2011, manual 2nd edition 2012/13, PREVENT and Mindful Nation UK 2015, IPD meta-analysis 2016, digital trial 2020, NICE NG222 2022. PubMed output rose to about 100-120 records a year by 2020 and has plateaued. The general mindfulness media peak around 2015-2016 comes from standard accounts; Google Trends and Reddit could not be checked because automated access is blocked. Reach combines publisher sales claims (checked 2026-10-13) with an unpublished, estimated course-completer count.
